incidents.vector: After exploiting a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day, the group moved laterally to an internal Linux appliance and used a custom Golang tool ("BONESAW") to exploit a new vCenter zero-day (CVE-2026-123890), hijacking SAML tokens to forge SSO administrator access.
incidents.impact: Mandiant/GTIG confirmed the vCenter zero-day is already being exploited in the wild for credential theft, data exfiltration, and full environment compromise; Broadcom has released patches with no workaround.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed a test environment at Rakuten's Securities division.
incidents.impact: Data on more than 15 million customer accounts was stolen, including sensitive information for 4.4 million of them; Rakuten says passwords, PINs, and other authentication data were not taken.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached shared IT provider Wellington IT, which serves dozens of Irish credit unions.
incidents.impact: Sensitive data was stolen from almost 50 credit unions; several have notified the Irish government, while others learned of the breach from authorities rather than from Wellington IT itself.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached N-able's cloud platform and accessed its Mail Assure and SpamExperts servers.
incidents.impact: N-able says it found no evidence that customer details were stolen and is rebuilding the affected services.

incidents.victim: Ethiopian Airlines ShebaMiles loyalty program members
incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Hackers breached Ethiopian Airlines' ShebaMiles loyalty program and stole customer data.

incidents.vector: A brute-force attack over a weekend compromised user credentials on Germany's e-government identity platform.
incidents.impact: At least 10,000 user accounts were compromised; officials locked the affected accounts and are notifying owners.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: KPMG's Canadian division is notifying clients of a security breach; the company has not disclosed what happened.

incidents.vector: An attacker exploited a data analysis tool to access the platform's internal network and copy data from its databases.
incidents.impact: Stolen data includes user details and their activity on the AI/coding learning platform; CodinGame has notified affected members.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: EV charging station app Chargemap is notifying customers of a security breach; details of the incident have not been made public.

incidents.vector: The Gentlemen ransomware cartel listed NVIDIA on its dark web leak site; the claim has not been verified.
incidents.impact: NVIDIA has not confirmed any security breach; if substantiated, the listing would represent a major ransomware claim against a leading chipmaker.

incidents.victim: Oil & gas, healthcare, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, and logistics firms (Warren Oil, Maxxis International-USA, Newpark Resources, Quantum Health, and ~24 others)
incidents.vector: Social engineering: callers posed as IT help desk staff to trick employees into giving up login credentials or installing remote access tools, then deployed ransomware and stole data for double extortion.
incidents.impact: A 60-plus-member network with ties to the former Conti gang extorted at least 28 companies for a combined $40.5 million; Ukrainian police, working with the FBI, arrested four alleged leaders and seized cash and devices, but say the wider network remains at large.

incidents.victim: Equinor and Skagerak Energi (Norwegian energy companies)
incidents.vector: Not yet disclosed; both companies report the attacks hit internal IT systems rather than operational technology.
incidents.impact: Two billion-dollar Norwegian energy firms disclosed cyberattacks on consecutive days; both say oil/gas production and power generation were unaffected, but internal email and business systems were disrupted, prompting other Norwegian energy firms to raise their alert posture.

incidents.vector: Attackers used the open-source ARTEX AI hacking platform to breach Commission systems beginning around Oct. 22, 2026.
incidents.impact: Payroll, leave requests, medical reimbursements, and translation services on the Sysper HR platform were disrupted for more than 10 days; the Commission found no evidence of a broad staff data breach or ransom demand, and the investigation remains open.

incidents.victim: Rocket Mortgage LLC and Mr. Cooper (Nationstar Mortgage)
incidents.vector: Threat actors impersonated Mr. Cooper employees on phone calls to trick the company's IT help desk into issuing temporary passwords, bypassing multi-factor authentication to access systems.
incidents.impact: A 2023 breach exposed large amounts of private customer information; NY DFS fined Rocket Mortgage and Mr. Cooper a combined $6.75 million for MFA and late-incident-reporting failures.

incidents.victim: American and European victims of Southeast Asian scam compounds
incidents.vector: Scam-compound operators in Cambodia and Burma ran virtual-currency investment fraud schemes against Americans and Europeans, protected by armed groups including the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army.
incidents.impact: Treasury's OFAC sanctioned scam-center operator Zhao Hui, two affiliated companies, and DKBA commanders for facilitating cyber-enabled investment fraud targeting U.S. citizens.

incidents.victim: Two unnamed US organizations (government/defense-contractor and nonprofit-adjacent)
incidents.vector: The group used data stolen from a 2025 cloud-account compromise — emails, passwords, and personnel records — to impersonate a trusted employee over an encrypted messaging app and send a malicious phishing link to a second organization.
incidents.impact: Google/Mandiant reports the group (tracked as Cold Relic/ColdRiver) downloaded large volumes of cloud storage data at the second organization and remains an active threat, with new phishing activity observed as recently as November 2026.

incidents.victim: Employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company (reportedly Palantir)
incidents.vector: A Russian national recruited via Telegram entered the U.S. illegally, used fraudulent identification and electronic surveillance equipment, and conducted in-person surveillance and stalking of company employees near their offices and homes.
incidents.impact: DOJ indicted Igor D'iu for acting as an unregistered Russian agent targeting a company supplying weapons used in Ukraine; he faces up to 10 years in prison and remains in federal custody.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained unauthorized access to two of Japan's national supercomputers.
incidents.impact: Stolen data included registered-user details, research data from home directories, and SSH keys used to connect the supercomputers to outside services.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached a third-party vendor that provides SharePoint data-migration services to Infoblox and stole customer data from it.
incidents.impact: Cybersecurity firm Infoblox is notifying customers of the breach; the number of affected customers and whether extortion was involved have not been disclosed.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed; breach affected the company's official website in October 2026.
incidents.impact: Fandango notified customers and state authorities of the breach; the scope of compromised data has not been made public.

incidents.vector: Not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Coles disclosed a security breach; the company says no data has been confirmed stolen so far but acknowledges that could change.

incidents.victim: At least 12 Dutch websites (sports and recreation sector)
incidents.vector: An advertising partner serving the sites ran malicious ads containing code designed to collect identifying data from older iPhone models.
incidents.impact: The affected sites warned users of the malicious ads; the incident mirrors the broader rise in ad-network and script supply-chain compromises seen this month.

incidents.victim: 178+ organizations including CNN, BBC, Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, Salesforce, GitLab, and NPR
incidents.vector: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into customer accounts, served from Optimizely's own trusted CDN under its legitimate certificate.
incidents.impact: The malware swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses, skimmed payment card data, stole cookies and screenshots, and pushed Coruna/DarkSword iOS exploit kits; Optimizely patched the flaw and removed the code, with roughly $7,500 in cryptocurrency confirmed stolen.

incidents.victim: ~1.3 million Android TV set-top box owners worldwide (XCPE botnet)
incidents.vector: Chinese device manufacturer Videostrong Technology shipped Android TV set-top boxes with built-in backdoor malware, which enrolled devices into a botnet and resold victims' internet connections to residential-proxy services.
incidents.impact: Google worked with industry partners to dismantle the XCPE botnet, severing access to more than 1.3 million directly infected boxes and an estimated 10 million additional connected IoT devices used for ad fraud and anonymized malicious traffic.
